en.headline: Motionless rat filmed lying on the floor inside Tai Wo Plaza in Tai Po
en.dek: A video shared in a local Facebook group on Tuesday showed a rat lying still with its eyes open as shoppers walked past, drawing comments about the mall's hygiene.
body: A video circulated online on Tuesday showed a rat lying motionless on the floor of Tai Wo Plaza in Tai Po, with its eyes open while a student filmed it and other shoppers walked by without reaction.

The footage was posted in the Facebook group Tai Po TAI PO, with the caption suggesting the mall had introduced Disney. Commenters noted the nearby market and said rats had appeared in the same spot last month, while some joked that the animal appeared to be choosing which of three nearby restaurants to visit.

Hong Kong has seen multiple recent reports of rats in public places, including at the Tsim Sha Tsui Cultural Centre and other districts. The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department has previously said it is stepping up monitoring and control measures in response to public complaints.
No official statement from the mall management or the department specifically addressing the Tai Wo Plaza incident had been issued by early Wednesday.

zh.headline: 大埔太和廣場老鼠躺地一動不動 途人淡定走過
zh.dek: 周二有網民在Facebook群組上載影片，顯示一隻老鼠躺在太和廣場地面，雙目打開，女學生拍攝期間其他途人照常經過。
body: 周二有網民在Facebook群組「大埔 TAI PO」上載影片及圖片，顯示大埔太和廣場內一隻老鼠躺在地面，完全沒有移動，雙目打開，一名女學生站在旁邊用手機拍攝，其他途人則淡定走過。
帖文戲稱「太和商場已引入迪士尼」。網民留言指隔鄰就是街市，是老鼠天堂，又有人說上個月中在同一位置見過老鼠，亦有人開玩笑說老鼠可能正在選擇附近三間食肆中哪一間開餐。
本港近期多區包括尖沙咀文化中心等地方都有鼠蹤報告。食物環境衞生署早前表示已加強監察及滅鼠工作，應對公眾投訴。
截至周三凌晨，暫未見商場管理公司或署方就太和廣場這宗事件發出正式回應。
